editorial:
Imagine a cop who is actually worse than the criminals he is supposed to catch. That is exactly who you get with Inspector Balboss. He is a greedy, dishonest guy who knows every dirty trick in the book. When he runs into a young homeless kid on the street, he doesn't try to help him get a job or a home. Instead, he decides to mentor the kid in the art of the scam. It is a weird, funny, and gritty look at the underworld where the line between the law and crime is totally blurred. You will find yourself rooting for these bad guys because they have a strange kind of chemistry together.

The acting is the best part here because it feels very real and grounded. While the pacing starts a bit slow, it picks up as the scams get bigger and riskier. Some of the older scenes feel a bit dated, but that just adds to the vintage charm. If you love old-school crime stories, you should definitely check this out. You can grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend.
endingExplained: In the end, the student becomes the master. The young man uses the very tricks Balboss taught him to double-cross the inspector. After a series of risky heists, the kid manages to steal the bulk of the money and disappear. Balboss is left with nothing, realizing he was too confident in his own cleverness. He ends up alone and broke, proving that in a world of thieves, the smartest one always wins.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old French crime films and stories about unlikely mentors.
